transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-01 10:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Recording: auto-recorded via Fireflies
Attendees: Marissa Chen (Redwood AE), Darren Cole (Redwood SE), Tom Rivera (NimbleCare Eng Lead), Simone Patel (NimbleCare SRE), Laila Gomez (NimbleCare PM)

Summary: short walk through of last week's burst of timeouts and 5xxs during a 30-minute test window; focused on where the throttles triggered, whether client retry patterns amplified the windowing, and short-term mitigations to keep the pilot healthy. Agreement to run client-side smoothing and increase certain timeouts on canary.

Topics: observed burst, rate-limiter windowing, retry budgets, exponential backoff jitter, timeout thresholds, KV cache prefixing, benchmark artifact links, next-steps for pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Marissa Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is the weekly POC sync, we'll focus on that spike you saw on Tuesday, right? The burst where a bunch of calls started timing out and then we saw 502/503s cascade.
[00:15] Tom Rivera: yep, thanks. We saw a hard bump, we were ramping test traffic, so it's probably our load but it turned into a long tail. Simones on the logs, she can walk through it.
[00:30] Simone Patel: yeah so 10:02 to 10:10 we had a big concentration, p95 went from 180ms to 2.1s and then the Redwood endpoint started returning 502 and occasional 503s. There were also client retries, which some of our infra folks think made the queue backlog worse.
[00:48] Darren Cole: just to clarify, the 502s — those were coming from the inference layer queuing out and hitting the gateway's circuit breaker, not from model OOMs. We saw the serving runtime evict some K-V cache entries under pressure. Sometimes the logs label that as "k v cache miss" which confuses the search.
[01:10] Laila Gomez: small question — were the retries immediate or with backoff? Our test harness was using a simple 1s retry with 3 attempts by default.
[01:22] Tom Rivera: yeah the harness did 1s fixed retry, so probably created a rhythm. Our intention was to test resilience but maybe we picked the wrong backoff.
[01:33] Simone Patel: the pattern was mostly clustered retries at 1s intervals, that produced short, high-amplitude spikes. The Redwood telemetry shows the rate limiter moved from 200 rps to a hard window once the token bucket emptied; then the adaptive fallback kicked in but that added latency as requests queued.
[01:55] Marissa Chen: ok so two levers: client-side smoothing (token-bucket or leaky bucket) and server-side policies (bigger bucket, softer windowing, or faster shed). Darren can you outline the immediate config knobs we can tweak?
[02:10] Darren Cole: sure. Short list: increase request timeout on the gateway from 10s to 20s for the canary route so long-running prompts don't get cut; relax the rate-limiter burst size for the pilot tenant (per-api-key quota); adjust backpressure to drop earlier with a 429 instead of letting it queue to 5xx; and enable prefix KV caching for the common prompt templates to reduce model compute.
[02:39] Tom Rivera: the timeout increase worries me a bit — I don't want requests sitting for 20s if they're going to fail. Would 15s be a safer first step?
[02:51] Darren Cole: 15s is reasonable. The main goal is to avoid premature timeouts that trigger retries. Also worth noting that some of the 502s are gateway timeouts where the SLO is short. We'll instrument to see if 15s captures most of the long tails.
[03:07] Simone Patel: action-wise, I'll flip the canary to 15s and we can compare error counts. Also, we found two request types that generate a lot of KV cache churn — large chat contexts with repeated system prompt tokens. If we prefix-hash those and cache the KV properly it drops token compute by about 20% per call in our tests.
[03:28] Laila Gomez: can you share that KV-cache tuning doc? We have a few prompts that are identical except for user variables.
[03:35] Marissa Chen: yes I'll share our KV-cache tuning note and a short guide on prefixing. Linking to the shared drive after the call.
[03:42] Tom Rivera: another angle — we use a small pool of dedicated API keys from our front end. Maybe per-user limits would help so one script doesn't burn the quota for everyone.
[03:55] Darren Cole: totally. Per-user versus per-tenant limits helps isolate noisy neighbors. For short-term pilot we can do per-api-key with a higher sliding window for internal tests, then shift to per-user once you onboard real traffic.
[04:12] Simone Patel: curious note — we saw a set of 5xxs that correlated with a specific model variant, labeled 'redwood-v2-small' in our logs. Could be a bad kernel path under that model, maybe quantization issues.
[04:26] Darren Cole: that's possible — sometimes the kernel selector picks an alternative kernel when sequence length is high. We'll correlate model variant + sequence length distribution. If it's reproducible, we can pin to the more stable runtime for the pilot.
[04:42] Tom Rivera: do you have any quick guardrails you'd recommend for our client retry policy? Current is 3 attempts with 1s fixed backoff.
[04:52] Marissa Chen: switch to exponential backoff with jitter, e.g., base 250ms, factor 2, max 4s, jitter 50-100%. Also implement retry budget: don't let retries exceed 30% of overall allowed requests in a window.
[05:10] Laila Gomez: that retry budget idea is new to some of our PMs, can you paste an example?
[05:16] Marissa Chen: yes — we'll include a simple spreadsheet. Darren: can you prepare an example budget calculation for 1k rps?
[05:22] Darren Cole: will do. Quick note — polite retries with jitter reduce pile-on significantly.
[05:27] Simone Patel: on observability, there was a gap: some of our upstream logs didn't include the runtime trace_id, so joining traces was painful. We should add a correlation header in the client.
[05:38] Marissa Chen: agreed. We'll put a recommended header X-Request-Trace and include it in our SDK snippet.
[05:44] Tom Rivera: two operational asks: can Redwood enable a quieter hour for the pilot so we can do bigger load tests? And can you share the benchmark spreadsheet you mentioned?
[05:55] Marissa Chen: yes we can set a temporary elevated burst window for your tenant for the test. I'll also drop the benchmark spreadsheet and the quiet-hour scheduling link in the follow-up.
[06:03] Laila Gomez: question re security — if we adjust timeouts or bump burst limits, does that change data residency or SOC2 footprint? Our InfoSec asked.
[06:13] Darren Cole: no, those are local runtime configs; they don't change where data sits. For SOC2/ISO concerns we'll share the compliance pack. If you need HSM/KMS integration for key management, that's separate and we can scope it.
[06:29] Simone Patel: we also want a list of which model variants are pinned for the pilot; if the unstable variant is involved we prefer to pin.
[06:36] Marissa Chen: under- stood. Darren will output a pin recommendation after correlating the model+seq length traces.
[06:44] Tom Rivera: re affinity — do you have a config to prefer lower-latency regional pools? Sometimes our traffic is US-east heavy and gets routed to different shards.
[06:55] Darren Cole: yes routing policy can prefer region, and we can route your pilot to an RU/US-east pool to reduce cross-region hops. That reduces variance.
[07:04] Laila Gomez: any cost implication for the increased burst window?
[07:09] Marissa Chen: if you keep it temporarily during testing we won't charge extra for the short experiment. Longer term, higher reserved capacity affects committed costs. AE can follow up with estimates.
[07:20] Simone Patel: small nit — in the telemetry we saw several misspellings of our service name which made filter rules miss some traces.
[07:27] Tom Rivera: yeah we had 'nimble-care' vs 'nimblecare' in different clients. We'll normalize that.
[07:33] Darren Cole: for the mitigation plan recap: 1) client smoothing via token bucket and exponential jittered backoff; 2) temporary increase of gateway timeout to 15s on canary; 3) enable prefix KV cache for heavy prompt templates; 4) optionally pin model variant or route to a stable runtime; 5) adjust rate-limiter to prefer 429 earlier than letting queue pressure create 502s.
[08:03] Marissa Chen: great, let's run through owners: Darren will grab p95/p99 traces and model-variant correlation; Simone will flip canary timeout to 15s and run two test passes; Tom will roll the client smoothing experiment on a feature flag to 10% then 50%; Marissa will send the docs and benchmark links.
[08:22] Laila Gomez: do we want to schedule a follow-up mid-week to see results?
[08:27] Marissa Chen: yes — same time next Wednesday 10am, I'll put it on calendar. If anything looks urgent we'll escalate earlier.
[08:34] Tom Rivera: quick question — regarding exponential backoff parameters do you recommend maximum attempts?
[08:40] Darren Cole: 4 attempts max is a common pattern. With jitter it's enough for transient failures without making a storm. Also implement a client-side quota so retries don't exceed a budget.
[08:53] Simone Patel: final note — we saw a handful of 5xxs under the 'redwood-v2-small' tag. If you can prioritize a quick kernel regression check that would help.
[09:02] Darren Cole: noted. I'll run a micro-benchmark across that variant and report results by Thursday.
[09:07] Marissa Chen: ok, thanks all. I'll follow up with the links, action items, and the quiet-hour scheduling form.
[09:15] Tom Rivera: thanks everyone.
[09:18] Laila Gomez: thanks.
[09:19] Simone Patel: bye.

End of transcript.
